about: Turnout by sector, Knesset elections 2013-2022, and 2026 expectations published before 2026-10-23 that are not vote-intention polls. Turnout = voters / registered. 'arab' = Arab and Druze localities (CBS locality religion code 2 or 3), the Dayan Center / IDI definition used in the literature (recomputed here from the CEC locality files; it matches the published 2022 counts exactly and the published percentages to 0.2 points). 'haredi' = Haredi cities only. 'generalImplied' = the rest. Built by scripts/forecast/round2/D2/build-turnout.mjs from turnout-cec.json (sector_turnout.py) and sector-gaps.json (gaps.mjs). See docs/research/polls-method/round2/D2-sector-data.md.

sources.cecLocalityResults: https://data.gov.il/dataset/votes-knesset (Central Elections Committee final results by locality, 19th-25th Knesset)
sources.overall: English Wikipedia election articles, {{Election results}} templates (CEC figures)

definitions.arab: Arab and Druze localities: registered voters and voters in localities the CBS classes as non-Jewish (2) or Bedouin tribes (3). Excludes mixed cities (Haifa, Jerusalem, Lod, Ramla, Akko, Tel Aviv-Jaffa, Nof HaGalil, Ma'alot-Tarshiha), Arabs living in Jewish localities and double envelopes. Druze localities are included (they vote mostly for Zionist lists). About 83-87% of all Arab-list votes are cast in these localities.
definitions.haredi: Haredi cities: Bnei Brak, Modi'in Illit, Beitar Illit, El'ad, Immanuel, Rechasim, Kiryat Ye'arim. About 3% of registered voters; 35-40% of UTJ's votes and 11-16% of Shas's are cast there.

haredi.note: Haredi cities only (Bnei Brak, Modi'in Illit, Beitar Illit, El'ad, Immanuel, Rechasim, Kiryat Ye'arim). Jerusalem, Beit Shemesh and other cities' Haredi neighbourhoods are not included; no published per-election Haredi-sector turnout series was found.

shasStrongholds.note: 11 Jewish non-Haredi localities, >=5,000 registered, Shas >=12% of valid votes in 2015: Beit She'an, Beit Shemesh, Dimona, Migdal HaEmek, Netivot, Ofakim, Or Yehuda, Kiryat Malachi, Tiberias, Yeruham, Safed. Beit Shemesh has a large Haredi population. turnoutMinusGeneralLocalities = stronghold turnout minus the general-sector locality turnout.

generalImplied.note: National minus Arab and Druze localities minus Haredi cities, with every double-envelope vote (soldiers, diplomats, prisoners, hospitals...) assigned to the general sector. Registered includes about 10% of voters living abroad, nearly all in this sector, so resident general-sector turnout is several points higher.

generalLocalitiesOnly.note: The same without double envelopes (locality ballot boxes only).

expectations2026.note: Published before 2026-10-23. None is an official forecast (the CEC publishes none). Items marked survey-based come from survey questions on turnout intention, not from vote-intention seat polls.

overall.what: Registered voters about 7.3 million; about 810,000 live abroad
Diplomatic-mission voting 86.7% (4,218 voters), up 17.1 points from 2022
Polymarket turnout market: 74%+ at 37%, 72-74% at 25% (thin market)
Next Data's CEC filings project 67.8% turnout by scaling 2022's 69.6%

arab.what: Stat-Net projects Arab turnout of 63% (vs 56% in 2022 on its own measure; 53.2% on the definition used here)
Konrad Adenauer Program (Dayan Center), May 2026: 53% expected as things stood, 67% if the Joint List reunited (Hadash-Ta'al-Balad did reunite in August; Ra'am runs separately)
Konrad Adenauer Program, Nov 2025: 52.4%, or 61.8% with a reunified list
Pre-election projections in 2022 were 40.5% (Makan), 49% (Konrad Adenauer Program) and below 40% (Al-Monitor); the result was 53.2%. Projections have missed by 4-13 points.

haredi.what: Gerrer Rebbe's directive to vote UTJ is a bare request, no mobilisation; UTJ officials fear Ger abstention (Ger is a large Hasidic court)
Shas rabbis campaign against defections to Likud and Otzma; UTJ builds a workaround for the ban on turnout data (booths, Agudah tents)
No numeric Haredi turnout projection was found. Haredi-city turnout has been 76-83% in every election since 2013 (this file).
